scope: model-independent authority and evidence boundary for consequential agent effects
claims_boundary: Conformance does not claim model accuracy, policy quality, physical correctness, or external audit.

requirements.title: Proposal is not authority
requirements.must: Model, planner, or agent output is treated as a proposal and cannot by itself authorize a consequential state or external effect.

requirements.title: Logical effect identity is runtime-owned
requirements.must: Canonical logical effect identity is allocated or validated by trusted runtime code and cannot be forged by model output.

requirements.title: Effect class is known before execution
requirements.must: The runtime distinguishes read-only from mutating or otherwise consequential effects before dispatch so policy, approval, and retry rules can be applied prospectively.

requirements.title: Authorization is explicit and separate
requirements.must: Intent, authorization, dispatch, acknowledgement, and observed outcome remain distinct lifecycle states; pending approval must not be represented as authorization or execution.

requirements.title: Transport evidence is not effect evidence
requirements.must: Successful dispatch or transport acknowledgement must not by itself prove that the intended external or physical effect occurred.

requirements.title: Unresolved outcome is first-class
requirements.must: When authoritative effect evidence is absent, stale, contradictory, or unavailable, the runtime preserves an unresolved state instead of inferring success or failure from transport behavior.

requirements.title: Retry identity prevents duplicate intent
requirements.must: Retries preserve one logical effect identity while attempts remain uniquely identifiable; retry handling must not silently create a second intentional mutation.

requirements.title: Compensation, when supported, is a distinct linked effect
requirements.must: A runtime may omit compensation. If compensation is supported, it must be represented as a distinct effect related to the original, and compensation requested, dispatched, acknowledged, and verified must not be collapsed into one state. A runtime that does not support compensation must not imply that reconciliation or retry is equivalent to rollback.

requirements.title: Fresh authoritative state closes the loop
requirements.must: A subsequent decision that depends on an external effect uses fresh authoritative state when required, rather than treating predicted, cached, or merely acknowledged state as physical truth.
